InstallCommand.RetireDirectory line 674 via SwapIntoPlace line 632. The existing doc comment on SwapIntoPlace asserts that renaming bin succeeds while h9k.exe runs from it because a rename is a directory-entry change, not a delete; the trace falsifies that on Windows, which locks the full path of a loaded module so a parent directory of a running exe cannot be renamed. Renaming the locked FILE itself is permitted. Fix shape: on Windows, retire per file (rename h9k.exe and any running h9kd.exe to .old names inside bin, move the staged files in beside them, sweep .old files on later runs, reusing the existing SweepRetiredDirectories best-effort pattern at file granularity); keep the directory swap on Unix where inode semantics make it correct. Consider the daemon: h9kd.exe running from bin has the same lock, so the update\\u0027s restart flow must stop it before the swap or rename its files the same way. A partial failure must leave bin runnable.
